# Equifax Provides Tips for College Students To Confidently Ace Credit 101


August 27, 2026


#### Story highlights:


-


For many, entering college is a first opportunity to build a credit history.


-


Students can establish healthy financial habits by paying balances on time and working to keep credit utilization below 30%.


-


Students can help protect their future by checking their credit reports on a regular basis and protecting important personal documents like Social Security cards.


-


By making required payments on student loans, college grads can keep building positive payment history.


College is an exciting time. But with that excitement comes new responsibilities, such as managing finances. For many college students, this means building a credit history. Understanding credit basics and adopting credit-building strategies can help facilitate long-term credit success.


#### Why Do Credit Scores Matter and How Are They Calculated?


A higher[credit score](https://www.equifax.com/personal/education/credit/score/articles/-/learn/how-is-credit-score-calculated/) can mean lower interest rates on mortgages and car loans, easier approval for renting a home and lower auto insurance rates. Factors considered in determining credit scores include payment history, credit utilization rate, and credit mix.


“Like so many goals in life, a successful financial journey starts with following a few key steps,” said Aparna Shah, Equifax Direct-to-Consumer Senior Vice President & General Manager. “Building a good credit score doesn’t have to be complicated, and college is a great time to build credit muscle that will last a lifetime.”


#### What Steps Can Help Build Credit?


When students arrive on campus, they may choose to apply for a credit card for the first time. A crucial step in establishing good credit is using any new card responsibly:


-


Balance expected income against necessary expenses to establish a reasonable budget.


-


[Consider a secured or student credit card](https://www.equifax.com/personal/education/credit-cards/articles/-/learn/establishing-credit-when-you-don-t-have-credit/) , which typically requires an upfront deposit.


-


Strive to pay off the balance in full and on time to avoid interest.


-


Work to keep the credit utilization rate at or below 30%. Always make the minimum monthly payment to keep the account in good standing.


-


Consider how much credit is needed before applying for multiple accounts, as hard inquiries can negatively affect scores.


#### How Can College Students Protect Their Identity?


Navigating enrollment paperwork and traveling to unfamiliar locations can heighten exposure to fraud and identity theft. Identity theft occurs when someone uses another person’s personal information to open lines of credit or receive insurance, housing, or employment — potentially affecting credit scores. To help prevent this:


-


Carry Social Security cards, birth certificates, or passports only when necessary.


-


If asked for a Social Security number, question why it’s needed and how it will be protected.


-


Check account statements regularly and be discreet when keying in PINs.


-


Access sensitive websites only from trusted devices on secure networks to prevent stolen login details.


-


Regularly review your Equifax credit report through the myEquifax™ app. Students can also use[Optimal Path](https://investor.equifax.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1393/equifax-delivers-optimal-path-directly-to-u-s-consumers) — the company’s free interactive credit score planner — on the myEquifax app to help build credit.


#### Do Student Loans Impact Credit?


For new students, graduation may seem like a distant goal. However for students financing their education via student loans, there will come a time when those loans must be repaid. Like all debt, student loans are a serious financial commitment that may impact credit scores depending on[how they are paid back](https://www.equifax.com/personal/education/loans/articles/-/learn/do-student-loans-affect-credit-scores/) . By making required payments on time, student loans can help build a person’s credit history.


Including these tactics in a payback strategy can continue credit momentum:


-


Make payments during the grace period to reduce interest on the loan.


-


Pay more than the minimum to lower the interest cost over time.


-


Consider enrolling in autopay to ensure timely payments, which may also reduce the interest rate.


-


If a minimum payment can’t be made, contact the lender immediately to explore repayment options or debt relief programs.


Building good credit in college can help lay the groundwork for a secure financial future. By practicing responsible borrowing, students can graduate with both a degree and a strong credit profile.
